lesson.picture: An interface is a job contract: 'must be able to Drive'. An abstract class is a half-built car chassis: engine already mounted, you add the body. You can sign many contracts, but you build on one chassis.
lesson.concept:
Interface = contract only: method signatures (and constants). A class may implement many. Use it when different, unrelated classes must be interchangeable — PaymentGateway implemented by Stripe, bKash, Nagad — and to decouple via dependency injection.

Abstract class = partial implementation: can hold properties, a constructor, concrete methods, plus abstract ones. A class extends only one. Use it when subclasses share real code and state — a BaseReport with formatting helpers, subclasses fill in fetchRows().

Senior rule: depend on interfaces at boundaries; use abstract classes to remove duplication inside a hierarchy. Prefer composition over deep inheritance.
lesson.bn: Interface = শুধু চুক্তি, কোনো code নেই, অনেকগুলো implement করা যায় — অচেনা class-গুলোকে অদলবদল করার জন্য (Stripe/bKash)। Abstract class = আধা-তৈরি class, property, constructor, শেয়ার করা method থাকে, একটাই extend করা যায় — subclass-গুলোর common code সরাতে। Boundary-তে interface, hierarchy-র ভেতরে abstract।

practice.task: Design the types: a NotificationChannel that can be Email, SMS or Push. Some share a formatMessage() implementation. What is an interface and what is abstract here? Write the skeleton.
Your Laravel controller type-hints PaymentGateway (an interface). Write the binding and say what happens if you forget it.

cards.q: Interface vs abstract class — three differences
cards.a: Interface: signatures only, no state, implement many. Abstract: properties/constructor/concrete methods, extend one, can mix abstract + concrete.

cards.q: When do you choose an interface?
cards.a: When unrelated classes must be swappable behind one contract, and for DI/testing (bind interface to a fake).

cards.q: When do you choose an abstract class?
cards.a: When subclasses share real code and state — a template method pattern: base does the flow, subclasses fill one step.

cards.q: What is 'composition over inheritance' in one line?
cards.a: Build behaviour by injecting collaborators rather than deep extends chains; changes stay local and classes stay testable.

cards.q: How does Laravel resolve an interface type-hinted in a constructor?
cards.a: Through the service container: a bind()/singleton() in a service provider maps the interface to a concrete class; the container reflects the constructor and injects it.
